independent_models.CH01-MINI01: The man was in/on the sea and is now in the dwelling. The fish are in the dwelling and are the man’s food. The dwelling is on the earth and is the man’s dwelling. Hē=mann, hīe=fiscas, hit=hof. Hīe is plural, męte is singular mass predicate; sindon agrees with hīe. Mannes is the possessor.
independent_models.CH01-MINI02: The creature was in the dwelling; it was an animal. The seed was in the dwelling; it was the creature’s food. Present: Sēo gesceaft is on ðǣm hofe. Hēo is dēor. Ðæt sǣd is on ðǣm hofe. Hit is ðǣre gesceafte męte. Plural first two: Ðā gesceafta sindon on ðǣm hofe. Hīe sindon dēor. Hēo reflects feminine gesceaft, not sex; hit refers to sǣd; gesceafte is G sg.
independent_models.CH01-READ01: God is the subject; heofonan and eorðan are A singular objects. Heofonan is weak feminine singular, not the masculine plural. In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
independent_models.CH01-READ02: Earth was empty and void; darkness was over the surface of the deep. Wǣron agrees with plural ðīestru. Brādnesse is D sg head after supplied ofer; ðǣre nēowolnesse is G sg dependent.
independent_models.CH01-READ03: God’s spirit was borne/carried, contextually moved, over the waters. Wæteru is A pl here; selected D pl is wæterum.
independent_models.CH01-READ04: A command/wish: Let light come to be. Light was made. Geweorðe is supplied finite 3 sg present subjunctive, not a report of an existing fact.
independent_models.CH01-READ05: God then saw that it was good. Ðā is then; ðæt is conjunction that; hit refers to neuter lēoht.
independent_models.CH01-READ06: God separated ðæt lēoht (A n sg direct object) fram ðǣm ðīestrum (D pl separation). Hē refers to God.
independent_models.CH01-READ07: Light was called Day and darkness Night. God/he is the understood subject of hēt. The close says one day, not the ordinal first.
independent_models.CH01-READ08: In the beginning God created heaven and earth. Now the earth was empty and void; and darkness was over the surface of the deep; and God’s spirit was carried over the waters. God then said, “Let light come to be”; and light was made. God then saw that it was good; and he separated the light from the darkness. And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night. Then there came to be evening and morning: one day.
independent_models.CH01-REVIEW01: Dagas, hwalas, wæstmas. Dæg/hwæl alternate singular æ with plural a; wæstm retains æ before its cluster.
independent_models.CH01-REVIEW02: In/on the birds’ trees. Trēowum is D pl head after on; ðāra fugla is G pl dependent; ðāra agrees with fugla.
independent_models.CH01-REVIEW03: Steorran can be G/D/A sg or N/A pl. Ðæs steorran lēoht: star’s light, steorran G sg. Ðā steorran wǣron on ðǣm heofone: stars were in the sky, steorran N pl.
independent_models.CH01-REVIEW04: Ðā ðīestru sindon on ðǣm heofone. Ðæt lēoht wæs on ðǣm hofe. Se mann gedǣlde ðā fuglas fram ðǣm dēore. Direct object A pl; separation D n sg.
